# ColorMeUp LAB

> OKLCH color scale generator: lightness, chroma, hue and curve control, WCAG & APCA contrast checks, and export to Tailwind, CSS, SCSS and SVG. Free and open-source.

ColorMeUp LAB builds color scales directly in the OKLCH color space, so steps are perceptually uniform rather than converted from hex or HSL. It previews colors in wide-gamut P3, supports up to ten base colors per palette, checks contrast, and exports to code. Every feature is free — there is no paywall. The palette lives in the URL, so any palette is shareable by link.

## Pages

- [Color palette generator](https://lab.colormeup.co/p): The main tool — create and fine-tune OKLCH color scales with control over lightness range, lightness curve, chroma curve, and hue shift.
- [OKLCH vs HSL](https://lab.colormeup.co/oklch-vs-hsl): Why OKLCH produces better scales than HSL.
- [Custom color scales](https://lab.colormeup.co/custom-color-scales): Building custom color scales for a design system.
- [Color scale vs palette](https://lab.colormeup.co/color-scale-vs-palette): How a scale differs from a palette, and six scale generators compared side by side.
- [About](https://lab.colormeup.co/about): What the tool is, how it works, and the OKLCH approach.

## Key facts

- Color space: OKLCH (perceptually uniform), with wide-gamut P3 preview.
- Pricing: free and open-source, no account required to use the generator.
- Export targets: Tailwind 4, Tailwind 3, CSS, SCSS, and SVG — each in OKLCH, HEX, HSL, or RGB notation.
- Contrast: WCAG 2 and APCA (WCAG 3) contrast grid.
- Charts: lightness, chroma, and hue plotted per scale, so uneven steps are visible.
- Scale presets: Tailwind, Material, Bootstrap, and Open Color.
- Also: color groups, live component and typography preview, per-color curve overrides, and saved palettes with an account.
- Built with the [colorizr](https://github.com/gilbarbara/colorizr) library.

## Palette URLs

A palette is fully encoded in the URL — one path segment per color, in order:

```
https://lab.colormeup.co/p/{Name}-{L}_{C}_{H}/{Name}-{L}_{C}_{H}
```

`L` is lightness 0–100, `C` is chroma, `H` is hue 0–360 (OKLCH). Example:

```
https://lab.colormeup.co/p/Primary-60_0.21_150/Secondary-60_0.139_227/Tertiary-60_0.266_304
```

Optional query params — all have defaults, and invalid values are ignored:

- `i` — steps, 3–20 (default 11)
- `m` — mode: `l` light (default), `d` dark, `r` reversed
- `v` — variant: `deep`, `neutral`, `pastel`, `subtle`, `vibrant`
- `f` — lightness curve, 0.1–5 (default 1.3)
- `c` — chroma curve, 0–1 (default 0)
- `h` — hue shift, -90 to 90 (default 0)
- `n` / `x` — min/max lightness, 0–1 (defaults 0.26 / 0.97)
- `s` — saturation, 0–100, with `o=1` to apply it to all colors
- `k` — lock a step, e.g. `k=500`
- `name` — palette name

The same short keys override options for a single color, comma-separated on that color's segment: `/p/Primary-60_0.21_150-x:0.95,m:d,g:b`. Color groups ride in that same chunk under `g:`, with the codes `b` (brand), `n` (neutral), `s` (semantic), and `d` (decorative).
